name: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
analogy: Think of it as a trader who tunes his rules by reviewing a random handful of 256 recent bars each evening instead of the whole history. Each review gives a slightly noisy hint on which way to adjust, but hundreds of cheap hints add up to the same improvement as one slow full review.

steps.title: Draw a small random batch
steps.description: Instead of using every training example, grab a small random batch. The batch is a rough but fair sample of the whole, so what it says on average is true of the full data.
steps.inExample: From 400,000 training bars a batch of 256 bars is drawn at random. Bars come only from the training window, never from the validation or test period.

steps.title: Predict and measure the batch error
steps.description: The model makes a prediction for each bar in the batch and the error is averaged over just those bars.
steps.inExample: The 256 predicted probabilities are compared with whether each bar actually closed higher 6 bars later, giving a batch loss of 697 thousandths.

steps.title: Estimate the tilt from the batch
steps.description: Work out, for every weight in the model, which way a nudge would reduce this batch's error. The result is noisy but points downhill on average.
steps.inExample: The network's 20,000 weights each get a nudge direction from this one batch; most are tiny and a few are large.

steps.title: Smooth with momentum
steps.description: Blend the new nudge with a running average of earlier nudges. Random jitter from small batches tends to cancel while the steady direction builds up.
steps.inExample: With a momentum of 90 percent, a weight that was pushed up in the last six batches keeps moving up even if this batch pushes slightly down.

steps.title: Take a step and shrink the step size over time
steps.description: Every weight moves by its smoothed nudge times the learning rate. The learning rate is gradually lowered so that the noise settles into a fine adjustment late in training.
steps.inExample: The learning rate starts at 1 thousandth and is cut in half every 2 passes through the training bars.

steps.title: Check on held-out data and stop in time
steps.description: After each pass through the data, the model is scored on bars it never trains on. Training stops once that score stops improving, to avoid memorising the training set.
steps.inExample: One pass is about 1,563 batches; validation loss improves to 690 thousandths at pass 5 and stalls, so training stops there.

useFor.example: Fitting a long short-term memory network or a transformer that reads the last 60 MNQ 5-minute bars to give a probability of a higher close 6 bars later.

useFor.task: Training on data too large to hold at once
useFor.example: Learning from millions of 1-minute bars streamed from the data lake in chunks.

useFor.task: Updating a model as bars arrive
useFor.example: Nudging a model's weights with each new batch of live bars instead of retraining from scratch every night.
Teaching a small vector for each instrument or market regime together with the forecasting layer above it.

avoidWhen: The dataset is small enough to fit in memory and a closed-form fit exists; ordinary least squares or full-batch gradient descent is exact and has no step-size tuning.
The objective is not differentiable, such as a raw backtest profit; use a score-only search method like differential evolution or Bayesian optimization.

example.scenario: A researcher trains a small neural network on 400,000 MNQ 5-minute bars to estimate the probability that the close 6 bars later is higher. Training uses mini-batches of 256 bars and momentum.

input.summary: The training settings and one feature of the latest bar that the trained model will score.

fields.name: training bars
fields.meaning: Five-minute MNQ bars in the training window.

fields.name: batch size
fields.meaning: How many bars are used for each nudge.

fields.name: steps per pass
fields.meaning: Number of batches needed to cover the training bars once.

fields.name: starting learning rate
fields.meaning: Size of each step at the beginning of training.

fields.name: momentum
fields.meaning: Share of the previous smoothed direction carried into the next step.

fields.name: latest bar average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: One of the features describing the bar to be scored after training.

output.summary: The loss over training, the point training stopped, and a probability for the latest bar.

fields.name: first batch loss, in thousandths
fields.meaning: Loss on the first batch, close to the coin-flip level of 693.

fields.name: validation loss at the best pass, in thousandths
fields.meaning: Loss on held-out bars at pass 5, slightly below the coin-flip level of 693.

fields.name: passes trained
fields.meaning: Full passes through the data before the validation loss stopped improving.

fields.name: probability the close is higher 6 bars later
fields.meaning: The trained network's estimate for the latest bar.

example.reading: A validation loss only 3 thousandths under the coin-flip level means the network found a small lean. Judge it on the net result after trading costs on later folds, not on the loss alone. The noisy training curve is normal; a validation curve that rises while training loss keeps falling is the signal to stop.
